_note: Draft IMD job. Field names follow the IMD worker's TaskDescriptor / LotusJobRequest schemas; map them onto the public paid-posting API when it opens. `guidance` = skills/hunt/SKILL.md without its YAML front matter. <COMMIT> = the round's commit in this repository. <FOCUS> = one of: hook-deltas, lifecycle, perp-book, perp-requote, vault, rotation, registry-facet, genesis-nft, randomness, governance, seed-deploy, value-flow. Rotate it across the round's hunts, weighting toward new code (MAP.md stale/missing) and value at risk; delete the `Focus:` sentence to let the seat draw one at random.
objective: 🐸 Fren Review HUNT — pepes help pepes. The swarm red-teams the Magic Internet Frens Cauldron as its external audit. Focus: <FOCUS>. You are an attacker with flash-loan capital, many wallets, contracts you deploy and a position in every block: find where the money is and how to get it out, or how to stop everyone else getting theirs. Red-team every Solidity file in this repository outside test/, reference/, lib/ and tools/: theft, permanent lock or loss of funds, broken accounting, access-control bypass, or bricking a core flow (trading, relaunch, claims, withdrawals, liquidation, treasury rotation). Follow skills/hunt/SKILL.md: sweep all 10 clusters (hook, registry, pool, perp, rotation, nft, governance, seed, art, deploy), go deep on your focus, attack the invariants it lists, and use its playbook, MAP.md and map/<cluster>.json. ledger/LEDGER.md (issues and leads) and ledger/KNOWN.md are what is already known: confirm or refute, never re-report. Build with `forge build`. Prove each new finding with a local Foundry PoC under test/scratch/ on test/fren-review/FrenBase.sol that meets skills/hunt/SKILL.md's proof standard (outsider actors only, no storage writes, damage asserted in numbers, a control), and paste its source and [PASS] line into the reproduction. What you cannot prove is a lead in the coverage block, not a finding. Finding no vulnerability is an acceptable result when the coverage block shows the whole scope was attacked.
acceptanceCriteria: .imd-findings.json exists in the repository root and is valid JSON in the IMD findings shape; {"findings": []} is an acceptable result.

Every finding points its path and line at the root cause, uses the severity rubric in skills/hunt/SKILL.md, names the invariant it breaks, and has a reproduction that was run: exact inputs and call sequence, expected vs actual, and the PoC source with the command and result line.

PoCs meet the skills/hunt/SKILL.md proof standard: the attacker is outside the trust circle (no prank as owner, registry, hook, timelock or governance unless the finding is about that role skipping a guard), no vm.store / vm.etch on protocol contracts, damage asserted in numbers, and a control without the attack step.

No issue already in ledger/LEDGER.md is reported as a new finding (it is confirmed or refuted in the coverage block instead), and no OPEN or ACCEPTED-LOW item from ledger/KNOWN.md is re-reported without a new, higher impact.

The final message starts with the FREN-REVIEW v1 coverage block from skills/hunt/SKILL.md: a focus line, one line for each of the 10 clusters with a verdict (solid, suspect or exploitable), the number of entry points examined and the deepest attempt; unproven suspicions go in lead lines.
No tracked file is modified; scratch PoCs live only under test/scratch/.
No transaction is sent to any live network and no private key is used.
